\lcEntry{\lcRef{Lemma}{L:fock-form}{3.2.2}}{Gaussian cutoff form bound}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{With the lemma's hypotheses and nothing supplied, \lcRef{Equation}{E:fock-sandwich}{3.2.5}, in coefficient form and as an operator-norm bound with $A_0\ge0$ and $B$ bounded self-adjoint on the cutoff Hilbert space, uniformly in $\epsilon$, $m$ and the band, for finitely many real modes, Hermite degree at most $N$ in the $m$ multiplied coordinates, on a Fourier-side model.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The Fourier-side model is not identified with the physical-space operators.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Lemma}{L:interval-contractions}{3.3.1}}{Dimension-independent Gaussian contractions}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{With the lemma's hypotheses and nothing supplied, \lcRef{Equation}{E:interval-column}{3.3.1}, its band-compressed form, the phase-insertion bound $\sqrt{R_\alpha}\,\rho^{(\alpha-2)/2}$, the sandwich bound $R_\alpha\rho^{\alpha-4}$ with self-adjointness and \lcRef{Equation}{E:interval-fock}{3.3.2}, for finitely many real modes, on a Fourier-side model, without tensoring by another Hilbert factor.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The Fourier-side model is not identified with the physical-space operators.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Proposition}{P:masked-quotient-obstruction}{4.1.5}}{A physical mask need not preserve noise-null tests}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{The proposition, with its hypotheses, for the covariance functional: $\E W(F)^2$ is read as the covariance functional of the test $F$.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The noise $W$ is not constructed, and the identification of $\E W(F)^2$ with the variance of the noise is not formalized.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Proposition}{P:variational-unmasked-rate}{7.3.3}}{The unmasked Rayleigh rate}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{With the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, the statements about the Rayleigh supremum \lcRef{Equation}{E:variational-real-rayleigh}{7.3.4}: for $\lambda$ defined as its square root, a uniform positive floor, the Lipschitz bounds and $I_\Psi$ positive and finite.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The operator statements ($H_s$ self-adjoint, form domain $H^1$, spectral bottom $E_s$, $\lambda=\sqrt{-E_s}$) are not formalized.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Lemma}{L:variational-control-dilation}{7.3.5}}{Radon and Rayleigh dilation}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{The bijection and the four identities with the section's hypotheses (\lcRef{Hypothesis}{H:homog}{1.2.1}, $\Gamma\neq0$, $a=\alpha_0$) and nothing supplied, for the variance in its integral form and the rate defined as the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum \lcRef{Equation}{E:variational-real-rayleigh}{7.3.4}.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The identification of the variance and the rate with $\E W(\Psi)^2$ (\lcRef{Lemma}{L:compact-raw-profile}{6.3.6}) and $\sqrt{-E_s}$ (\lcRef{Proposition}{P:variational-unmasked-rate}{7.3.3}) is not formalized.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Proposition}{P:variational-positive-scores}{7.3.6}}{Intrinsic variational lower bounds}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{The proposition with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, including the boundedness of the value sets and the supremum statements ($S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}$ finite, positive, equal to $c^{(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)}S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$), with $\lambda$ the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum and $v_\Psi$ the cost in its integral form.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{$Q_2\ge S_2^{\mathrm{pos}}$ is not formalized.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Lemma}{L:spatial-static-controls}{8.2.2}}{Smooth temporal controls}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{$\lambda$ is the square root of the supremum of the real Rayleigh quotient, and $I_\Psi$, $v_\Psi$ are given by their integral formulas; \lcRef{Equation}{E:spatial-static-score}{8.2.2} is proved both in the form that every number below the bound is exceeded by some admissible score and in its supremum form, with nothing supplied.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The identifications of $\lambda$ with $\sqrt{-E_s}$ and of $v_\Psi$ with $\E W(\Psi)^2$ are not formalized.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Proposition}{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}{8.2.4}}{The finite smooth spatial ratio}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{\lcRef{Equation}{E:spatial-smooth-score}{8.2.4}, with nothing supplied, both in the form that every $y$ below the bound is exceeded by some $I_\Psi-v_\Psi/2$ and as a bound on the supremum, with $\lambda$ the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum and $v_\Psi$ given by its integral formula. $R_0<\infty$ is proved by \lcRef{Lemma}{L:spatial-fourier-bound}{8.2.3}.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The identification of $\lambda$ and $v_\Psi$ with $\sqrt{-E_s}$ and $\E W(\Psi)^2$ is not formalized.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Proposition}{P:spatial-energy-map}{8.2.6}}{The spatial energy and static lower variational expression}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{\lcRef{Equation}{E:spatial-static-energy-score}{8.2.10}, with nothing supplied, both in an existential form (every $y$ below $M_a^{-1/k}F_0(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}})$ is exceeded by some $I_\Psi-v_\Psi/2$) and in its supremum form, with $\lambda$ the square root of the Rayleigh supremum \lcRef{Equation}{E:variational-real-rayleigh}{7.3.4} and $v_\Psi$ by its integral formula.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The identification of $\lambda$ and $v_\Psi$ with $\sqrt{-E_s}$ and $\E W(\Psi)^2$ is not formalized.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Proposition}{P:cameron-temporal-map}{8.3.4}}{The compact temporal mean, without trace class}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{With nothing supplied, for $2<r<2/a$: $K$ is bounded, positive, strictly positive, injective and compact; a positive square root $K^{1/2}$ is compact; $\iota:H_t\to L^2(I)$ is onto and isometric with $\iota[f]=K^{1/2}f$; $C_t=K^{1/2}\iota$ is compact into $L^r(I)$, $C_tf=Kf$ on tests. The statements that $K$ is not trace class and that $C_t:H_t\to L^2(I)$ is not Hilbert--Schmidt are proved as cell-sum identities.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The two operator-class statements themselves are not formalized (Mathlib has no trace class).}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Proposition}{P:cameron-full-mean}{8.3.5}}{The compact time-space mean}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{Only the map $\mathcal{U}$, with nothing supplied, for $2<r<2/a$ ($H_I$ the kernel completion, M5), in two statements: for each temporal core a bounded $\mathcal{U}:H_I\to L^r(I;H_{\mathrm{sp}})$ with $\mathcal{U}(f\otimes q)(s)=(Kf)(s)q$ a.e.\ for time tests $f$ and $\|\mathcal{U}\|\le\|C_t\|$; separately, such a $\mathcal{U}$ with $\|\mathcal{U}\|\le\|K_a\|_{r/2}^{1/2}$.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The compactness of $T$, its multiplier formula and \lcRef{Equation}{E:cameron-compact-tail}{8.3.7} are not formalized.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Lemma}{L:uniform-mean-cutoff}{9.1.1}}{Uniform cutoff and physical mean}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{For every real $\sigma$ and $R\ge1$, a bounded operator on $H^\sigma$ agreeing with multiplication by $\eta_R$ on real tests, of norm at most $M_\sigma$ (tests are proved dense for $\sigma\le1$, covering the case $\sigma=1/2$ used), the embedding $H^s\to H^t$ of norm at most one for $t\le s$, and \lcRef{Equation}{E:uniform-spatial-mean}{9.1.2} for every $T$ with the row at all states.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{That this operator is the only bounded operator agreeing with multiplication by $\eta_R$ on real tests is not stated.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Lemma}{L:uniform-mean-tensor}{9.1.3}}{Dimension-free Hilbert tensor extension}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{The bound on finite tensors $\sum_jf_j\otimes e_j$ with orthonormal $e_j$, for complete real Hilbert spaces $H_0$, $G$ and $2\le r<\infty$ (Gaussian route, Step~1 by Parseval and Minkowski), and the non-compactness sentence as the identity $\|F_i-F_j\|=\sqrt2\|Af\|$.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The extension of $A\otimes I_G$ to the completed tensor product is not stated (Mathlib has no completed Hilbert tensor product).}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Lemma}{L:tube-closed-geometry}{10.2.2}}{Compact images and attained tube radii}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{With the lemma's hypotheses and nothing supplied, that every $\mathcal{T}_r$, $r\ge0$, is closed, the first identity $\{d_\delta\le r\}=\mathcal{T}_r$ of \lcRef{Equation}{E:tube-attained-radius}{10.2.4}, and that $d_\delta$ is lower semicontinuous.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The Gaussian tail $\mathbb{P}(d_\delta(X)>r)\le e^{-r^2/(2\delta)}$ and the almost sure finiteness of $d_\delta(X)$ are not formalized.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Lemma}{L:tube-rayleigh-tail}{10.2.7}}{Exact Rayleigh tail bound}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{The bound with integrability and the finite head integral.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The ``In particular'' application to the coarse-envelope bound of another proposition is not formalized.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Lemma}{L:uniform-E-lift}{10.3.1}}{Unique potential and fixed-radius lift}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{For every covariance and cutoff profile with nothing supplied, that for every $R\ge1$ each $L\in\mathcal{V}_{E,R}$ is $B_E(M)$ with $\|L\|=\|M\|$, and determines the unique real potential $V\in H^{-1/2}$ supported in $\operatorname{supp}m_R$ with $Mu=Vu$ on tests, and \lcRef{Equation}{E:uniform-E-pairing}{10.3.1} with its symmetry for real states.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The lift $L_F$ and the Hermitian extension to complex states are not formalized.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Lemma}{L:positive-physical-gram}{11.2.2}}{Finite covariance vectors and entrywise order}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{With the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, that $k_i^R$ and $k_i^\infty$ lie in $H_I$ (M5), that both Grams factor into the temporal pairing and $B_\Gamma$, and that both are positive semidefinite.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The label row \lcRef{Equation}{E:positive-label-row}{11.2.4} ($\mathcal{T}_R$, $v_L$ not constructed) and the entrywise order are not formalized.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Lemma}{L:occupation-raw-square}{11.3.1}}{Full-profile squares in the original space}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{With the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, $Q:H^1\to H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ with $\langle Q(f),Q(h)\rangle=B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)$, continuous on $H^1$ (M6), and for fields of $\mathcal{O}$ modelled by joint representatives $\rho_g\in H_I$ (M5) both identities of \lcRef{Equation}{E:occupation-raw-identities}{11.3.2} and $\langle\Psi,\rho_g\rangle\le\sqrt{v_\Psi A(g)}$.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{These identities and this bound are not restated on the class $\mathcal{O}$ itself.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Lemma}{L:occupation-rayleigh-selection}{11.3.3}}{Countable Rayleigh near-occupations}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{\lcRef{Equation}{E:occupation-rayleigh-selection}{11.3.6} with the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, with $g_\varepsilon$ in the class $\mathcal{O}$ itself (strongly $H^1$-measurable fields, read as a.e.-strongly measurable); $\lambda$ is the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum and $v_\Psi$ the integral-form cost.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The identification of $\lambda$ and $v_\Psi$ with $\sqrt{-E_s}$ and $\mathbb{E}W(\Psi)^2$ is not formalized.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Theorem}{T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling}{11.3.4}}{The computed occupation ceiling}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{With the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, for $\mathfrak{c}>0$: $\mathfrak{c}I_\Psi-v_\Psi/2\le U_{\mathfrak{c}}$ for nonnegative smooth controls, $S_{\mathfrak{c}}^{\mathrm{pos}}\le U_{\mathfrak{c}}$ with the exact $C_{\rm occ}$, and, for every $\zeta>0$, $U_{\mathfrak{c}}=\mathfrak{c}^m(2\zeta)^{\alpha/(2k)}F_0(\mathcal{E}_\zeta^{\mathcal{O}})$, over the class $\mathcal{O}$ itself; $\lambda$ and $v_\Psi$ in Rayleigh and integral form.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{$C_2(\Gamma,a)\le U_2$ is not formalized.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Corollary}{C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket}{11.3.5}}{A common spatial-energy bracket}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{With the section's hypotheses and nothing supplied, \lcRef{Equation}{E:intrinsic-spatial-bracket}{11.3.9} and the comparison $S_2^{\mathrm{pos}}\le2^mF_0(\mathcal{E}_{1/2}^{\mathcal{O}})<2^mF_a(\mathcal{E}_{1/2}^{\mathcal{O}})$ for the variational value $S_2^{\mathrm{pos}}$ in place of $C_2(\Gamma,a)$ (identified by \lcRef{Theorem}{T:intrinsic-second-moment}{11.2.6}), with $\mathcal{E}_{1/2}^{\mathcal{O}}$ over the class $\mathcal{O}$ itself; $\lambda$ is the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum.}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Proposition}{P:riesz-small}{A.1.3}}{Riesz finite coefficients}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{With nothing supplied, \lcRef{Equation}{E:riesz-two}{A.1.7} and the total $\E X_1^2+2\E X_2$ for the chaos terms of every source field, \lcRef{Equation}{E:riesz-two}{A.1.7} and $A_1=J_{1,1}+2J_{2,0}$ for the M4 diagrams, and \lcRef{Equation}{E:riesz-four}{A.1.8} with finiteness for all splits and pairings (density diagrams, equal to the limit diagrams).}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The multiplicities of \lcRef{Equation}{E:total-four}{A.1.3} are not formalized.}
\lcEntryEnd

\lcEntry{\lcRef{Proposition}{P:tube-rayleigh-transfer}{10.2.3}}{Comparison with the Rayleigh integral, including jumps and zero law}
\lcInputs{Input supplied}
\lcInput{1}{\texttt{TubeTail}: $\mathbb{P}(d_\delta(X)>r)\le e^{-r^2/(2\delta)}$ for $r\ge0$ (second part of \lcRef{Equation}{E:tube-attained-radius}{10.2.4}, proved there from the imported Gaussian isoperimetric theorem of Borell and Sudakov--Tsirelson; nonzero law only)}
\lcEntryEnd

\lcCategory{Steps checked, not the result itself; analytic inputs either supplied as hypotheses or left outside Lean.}{30}
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Lemma}{L:complex-phase}{3.2.1}}{A complex phase bound}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{With the lemma's hypotheses, the numerical-range and scalar steps on $W(L)$ with nothing supplied, and, with the inputs below, the bounds $3$, $6(1+\lambda h)$, $6$ (times $e^{\lambda h}$) for $C_h(L)$, $F_h(L)$, $H_h(L)$, the root comparisons $7/6$, $6/5$ and the bound $100e^{2\lambda h}$ for the weighted block map.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The identification of the weighted block map with $\mathcal{M}_z(h)$ is not formalized.}
\lcInputs{Inputs supplied}
\lcInput{1}{\lcRef{Equation}{E:cp-input}{3.2.1} (Crouzeix--Palencia, imported in the manuscript) for $C_h$, $F_h$, $H_h$ at $L=A_0-zB$ with its holomorphy precondition: operators of norm at most $(1+\sqrt2)M$ whenever the scalar function is bounded by $M$ on $W(L)$}
\lcInput{2}{the inverse-root integral representation in the proof of \lcRef{Lemma}{L:complex-phase}{3.2.1} for $L^*=A_0-\overline{z}B$ (bounded holomorphic calculus): $Q'-1=\pi^{-1}\int_0^\infty J(t)\ud t$ with $J$ strongly measurable and $\|J(t)\|\le(|z|d/(1-\delta_a))t^{-1/2}\kappa^{a-3}$}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Proposition}{P:static-phase-all-orders}{3.2.4}}{All regularized static phase orders}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{The Cauchy coefficient estimate, the arithmetic at $\lambda=n/h$ and the series bound of the proof, and from them both displays for abstract Banach-space quantities, with the circle bound (or the inputs of \lcRef{Lemma}{L:complex-phase}{3.2.1} and \lcRef{Equation}{E:fock-sandwich}{3.2.5}), entireness, the coefficient identification, the norm comparisons, the cutoff removals and the free bound supplied.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{Phases are not constructed.}

\lcInput{1}{the moment bound of \lcRef{Corollary}{C:radius-covariance-residuals}{9.2.4} (from \lcRef{Proposition}{P:radius-actual-moments}{9.2.3}) on the unstopped block paths: almost surely $C^\theta$, $p$-th norm power integrable, $(\E\|M_R(Y_m)\|^p)^{1/p}\le C\sqrt p\,R^{d/Q}$}
\lcInput{2}{measurability of the $C^\theta$ norm of the stopped block paths (implicit in the manuscript)}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Proposition}{P:signed-closed-form}{9.3.2}}{Closed form and quarter-power phase}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{For an abstract bounded Hermitian pairing on Mathlib's $H^1$ with \lcRef{Equation}{E:signed-multiplier-form}{9.3.1} supplied, \lcRef{Equation}{E:signed-form-bounds}{9.3.3}, the form version of $A\ge1$, the step $\|u\|_{H^{1/2}}^2\le bz$ and the bounded resolvent of the form (self-adjoint, positive, injective, norm at most $1$, unique weak solution).}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{$H_V$, $D(A^{1/2})=H^1$, \lcRef{Equation}{E:signed-quarter-phase}{9.3.4} and $H^{-1/2}$ are not formalized.}
\lcInputs{Inputs supplied}
\lcInput{1}{\texttt{SignedMultiplierForm P k}: \lcRef{Equation}{E:signed-multiplier-form}{9.3.1}, the conclusion of \lcRef{Lemma}{L:signed-limiting-multiplier}{9.3.1} (not formalized), for an abstract bounded operator $P$ on $H^1$ standing for the pairing $v_V$; the multiplier $V$ is not constructed}
\lcInput{2}{the self-adjointness of $P$: the Hermitian pairing of the proof of \lcRef{Lemma}{L:signed-limiting-multiplier}{9.3.1}}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Lemma}{L:symplectic-free}{10.1.1}}{Free wave form and compact Young baseline}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{Both compact-baseline displays on an abstract nonzero Hilbert space with a supplied free group, isometric velocity reversal and weakly vanishing translations, for a Young evolution given only by convergence of its left Young sums; and $W_t^{\mathsf{T}}J_{\rm symp}W_t=J_{\rm symp}$ per frequency and the force skewness for the $L^2$ pairing.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{$J_E$ and the preservation of $\omega$ on $E$ are not formalized.}
\lcInputs{Inputs supplied}
\lcInput{1}{the free wave group on $E=H^{1/2}\times H^{-1/2}$ with its group law, the isometric velocity reversal with $S_E(-h)=\mathcal{R}S_E(h)\mathcal{R}$, and the spatial translations, isometric, commuting with $S_E(h)$ and weakly null as $|y|\to\infty$ (in the proof of \lcRef{Lemma}{L:symplectic-free}{10.1.1}); $E$ is an abstract nonzero real Hilbert space}
\lcInput{2}{\lcRef{Proposition}{P:constant-young-linear}{6.2.4} on $\mathcal{L}(E)$ (in the proof of \lcRef{Lemma}{L:symplectic-free}{10.1.1}): the left Young sums of $X$ over partitions of $[s,t]$ converge in operator norm to $U_X(t,s)-I$; supplied in the weaker form of convergence along some nontrivial filter of finite node lists in $[s,t]$ (no ordering, endpoint or mesh condition)}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Proposition}{P:gram-positive-optimizer}{11.1.3}}{Positive conic maximizer}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{Only the finite, algebraic or scalar steps of this result listed in the companion's statement ledger.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The result itself.}
\lcPart{Assumptions and limits}{The checked step takes no analytic input beyond the paper's hypotheses: the Lean statement assumes only positive weights and active labels, $\langle\Phi,k_i\rangle-b_i\ge0$. Dual coercivity, the existence and uniqueness of the dual minimizer, attainment and the maximum over active sets are outside Lean (see the statement-ledger entry \texttt{PositiveGram}).}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Proposition}{P:gram-entrywise-comparison}{11.1.5}}{Entrywise Gram comparison}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{Only the finite, algebraic or scalar steps of this result listed in the companion's statement ledger.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The result itself.}
\lcPart{Assumptions and limits}{The checked step takes no analytic input beyond the paper's hypotheses: the Lean statement assumes only nonnegative weights and the entrywise order $C_{ij}\le D_{ij}$, a hypothesis of \lcRef{Proposition}{P:gram-entrywise-comparison}{11.1.5}. The Gram realization (\lcRef{Lemma}{L:gram-realization}{11.1.4}) and the optimization over weights are outside Lean (see the statement-ledger entry \texttt{PositiveGram}).}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Proposition}{P:white-spatial-energy}{11.4.2}}{Exact white spatial energy}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{Only the finite, algebraic or scalar steps of this result listed in the companion's statement ledger.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The result itself.}
\lcInputs{Input supplied}
\lcInput{1}{The Lean statements take as hypothesis: (1) the inequality \lcRef{Equation}{E:white-cdf-square}{11.4.1} of \lcRef{Lemma}{L:white-cdf-square}{11.4.1}, $0\le b-2zA+z^2/3$ for every real $z$, with $A=\int_\R f^4$ and $b=\int_\R(f')^2$ for a real unit $f\in H^1(\R)$ (hypothesis \texttt{h} of \texttt{WhiteCDF.cdf\_square\_bound}). The bound $3A^2\le b$ that \texttt{WhiteCDF.energy\_upper} assumes is the conclusion of \texttt{cdf\_square\_bound}. The white-model statements assume only $c\ge0$, and $0<a<1$ for \lcRef{Hypothesis}{H:homog}{1.2.1}. The variational energy, its domain and its attainment are outside Lean (see the statement-ledger entries \texttt{WhiteCDF} and \texttt{WhiteModel}).}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Theorem}{T:white-moment-bounds}{11.4.3}}{Explicit white moment bounds}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{\lcRef{Equation}{E:white-moment-bounds}{11.4.2} for the variational value $S_2^{\mathrm{pos}}$ in place of $C_2(c,a)$ (identified by \lcRef{Theorem}{T:intrinsic-second-moment}{11.2.6}), for $c>0$ and $0<a<1$, with the value $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}=c^2/6$ of \lcRef{Proposition}{P:white-spatial-energy}{11.4.2} supplied (each bound uses one inequality of it), and that $M_a$, $K_0(a)$ and both bound formulas are positive.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The time exponent sentence and the case $c=0$ are not formalized.}
\lcInputs{Input supplied}
\lcInput{1}{\lcRef{Proposition}{P:white-spatial-energy}{11.4.2}: the spatial energy of $c\delta_0$ is $c^2/6$ for $c>0$; the lower bound uses only $c^2/6\le\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}$ (the sech profile), the upper bound only $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}\le c^2/6$ (the CDF square, \lcRef{Equation}{E:white-cdf-square}{11.4.1}); not proved}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Corollary}{C:three-product-riesz}{C.2.6}}{Ordinary product and Riesz covariances in dimension three}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{With the corollary's hypotheses, that the product and Riesz targets are nonzero covariances with scaling $3-\alpha$ whose endpoints satisfy \lcRef{Hypothesis}{H:three-endpoints}{C.2.2}, and, from the supplied \lcRef{Proposition}{P:three-transfer}{C.2.5}, the coefficient, moment and asymptotic bounds for an abstract model of $A_k(t)$, $\E u^2$ and $\mathcal{M}_{\rm st}$; the asymptotic bound is for every spectral measure of the low endpoint.}
\lcInputs{Input supplied}
\lcInput{1}{\texttt{ThreeTransfer}: the exact statement of \lcRef{Proposition}{P:three-transfer}{C.2.5} (proved in the manuscript) for an abstract \texttt{ThreeMomentModel} at the midpoint $\vartheta$; true for the manuscript's $A_k(t)$, $\E u^2(t,x)$ and $\mathcal{M}_{\rm st}$, which the package does not construct}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Corollary}{C:three-finite-images}{C.2.7}}{Finite sums of linear images}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{With the corollary's hypotheses, that $\sum_iw_i(T_i)_\#\Gamma_i$ is a nonzero covariance with scaling $3-\alpha$ whose endpoints satisfy \lcRef{Hypothesis}{H:three-endpoints}{C.2.2}, and, from the supplied \lcRef{Proposition}{P:three-transfer}{C.2.5}, the coefficient, moment and asymptotic bounds for an abstract model of $A_k(t)$, $\E u^2$ and $\mathcal{M}_{\rm st}$; the asymptotic bound is for every spectral measure of the low endpoint.}
\lcInputs{Input supplied}
\lcInput{1}{\texttt{ThreeTransfer}: the exact statement of \lcRef{Proposition}{P:three-transfer}{C.2.5} (proved in the manuscript) for an abstract \texttt{ThreeMomentModel} at the midpoint $\vartheta$; true for the manuscript's $A_k(t)$, $\E u^2(t,x)$ and $\mathcal{M}_{\rm st}$, which the package does not construct}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Proposition}{P:moment-growth-logconvex}{D.1.7}}{Log-convexity of the upper growth type}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{Every conclusion, for an abstract moment function with the supplied coefficient, interpolation, static-law, minorant and upper-bound facts.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The moments $\E u^{(a)}(T,x)^p$ of the solution are not constructed, so their identification with that function is not formalized.}
\lcInputs{Inputs supplied}
\lcInput{1}{\lcRef{Equation}{E:static-ratio-input}{D.1.1} (Chen--Hu static law): $0<L_0$ and $T^{-\kappa_{\rm st}}\log\E U(T,x)^p\to p^{\kappa_{\rm st}}L_0$ for $p=1,2$ (fields \texttt{L0\_pos}, \texttt{static\_law})}
\lcInput{2}{\lcRef{Equation}{E:full-moment-positive-series}{D.1.11} of \lcRef{Lemma}{L:full-moment-coefficient-holder}{D.1.6} with $c_{p,0}(a)=1$ (\lcRef{Equation}{E:full-moment-coefficients}{D.1.10}), nonnegative coefficients, summable for $t>0$, $0\le a<a_{\max}$ (field \texttt{series})}
\lcInput{3}{\lcRef{Equation}{E:full-moment-coefficient-holder}{D.1.12} of \lcRef{Lemma}{L:full-moment-coefficient-holder}{D.1.6} (field \texttt{holder})}
\lcInput{4}{\lcRef{Equation}{E:static-minorant-rate}{D.1.6} of \lcRef{Proposition}{P:static-minorant-lower}{D.1.3}, as: every $y<p^{\kappa_{\rm st}}L_0$ is eventually below $T^{-\kappa(a)}\log\E u^{(a)}(T,x)^p$, $0<a<a_{\max}$ (field \texttt{minorant})}
\lcInput{5}{\lcRef{Equation}{E:full-upper-bound}{3.3.28} of \lcRef{Theorem}{T:full-upper}{3.3.8} at temporal exponent $a$: $\E u^{(a)}(T,x)^2\le e(T+2)^d\exp(CT^{\kappa(a)})$ for $T\ge1$, one finite $C$ (field \texttt{full\_upper})}
\lcInput{6}{Cauchy--Schwarz $(\E u^{(a)}(T,x))^2\le\E u^{(a)}(T,x)^2$ (field \texttt{cauchy\_schwarz}; in the proof of \lcRef{Proposition}{P:moment-growth-logconvex}{D.1.7})}
\lcEntryEnd
\lcEntry{\lcRef{Corollary}{C:static-moment-constant-continuity}{D.1.8}}{Recovery of the static moment constant}
\lcPart{Lean proves}{Every conclusion, for an abstract moment function with the supplied facts of the logconvexity proposition and the static minorant and law.}
\lcPart{Not yet formalized}{The moments of the solution are not constructed, so their identification with that function is not formalized.}
\lcInputs{Inputs supplied}
\lcInput{1}{\lcRef{Equation}{E:static-minorant-rate}{D.1.6} of \lcRef{Proposition}{P:static-minorant-lower}{D.1.3} (field \texttt{minorant}) and $\overline{\Lambda}_p(0)=C_p$ from \lcRef{Equation}{E:static-ratio-input}{D.1.1} (fields \texttt{L0\_pos}, \texttt{static\_law})}
\lcInput{2}{the inputs of \lcRef{Proposition}{P:moment-growth-logconvex}{D.1.7}: \lcRef{Equation}{E:full-moment-positive-series}{D.1.11} and \lcRef{Equation}{E:full-moment-coefficient-holder}{D.1.12} of \lcRef{Lemma}{L:full-moment-coefficient-holder}{D.1.6} (fields \texttt{series}, \texttt{holder}), \lcRef{Equation}{E:full-upper-bound}{3.3.28} of \lcRef{Theorem}{T:full-upper}{3.3.8} (field \texttt{full\_upper}), Cauchy--Schwarz (field \texttt{cauchy\_schwarz})}
\lcEntryEnd

\newcommand{\lcModelKey}{%
\item[M1] In dimension three the wave Green measure is defined through Mathlib's sphere measure; that it equals the surface measure used in the text is not proved in Lean.
\item[M2] The Gaussian space over finitely many coordinates is represented by normalized Hermite coefficient vectors; that Bochner integrals in it agree with the coordinatewise integrals is not proved in Lean.
\item[M3] The smoothed covariance $p_\varepsilon*\Gamma$ is taken as the measure with density $\gamma_\varepsilon$; that it equals Mathlib's convolution of measures is not proved in Lean.
\item[M4] The two-chain diagram integrals are the deterministic integrals of a diagram model; the identification of their increment form with the positions form in the text is not proved in Lean for the wave Green measure of dimension three (the sphere measure of M1) (it is proved in dimension one and, for a measurable covariance and Green measures with a finite jointly measurable density, in every dimension).
\item[M5] The completion spaces $H_t\otimes G$, $H_t$, $H_I$ and $H_\Gamma$ are realized as $L^2$ completions under the kernel and covariance forms; no tensor-product identification and no isometry between $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ and $H_\Gamma$ is proved in Lean.
\item[M6] $H^1$ is the graph of the weak gradient in $L^2\times L^2$, with the topology of Mathlib's $H^1$; that every real element of Mathlib's $H^1$ arises from it is not proved in Lean.
}
